Subject: Clarify minimums & rounding for long-context inference

Hey Camila,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the latency and KV reuse looked great. Before procurement drafts a PO, legal asked a few concrete billing clarifications we need in the SOW:

1) If a single API call includes a 50k-character context (we have docs + product metadata) and generates a 400-token completion, how do you apply minimums/rounding? Do you meter on raw tokens, or do you bucket by request and apply a per-call floor?

2) We expect a mix of long prepended context + short user queries. Will prefix caching reduce billable tokens automatically, or is there any required session/handle to enable KV reuse?

3) Wanted to confirm whether anchor credits (you mentioned a one-time credit for onboarding) can be applied against month 1 overage vs across a 3-month ramp.

Procurement copied procurement@beaconretail.com.

Appreciate a short write-up we can attach to the SOW.

— Ellie

Hi Ellie — great follow-up and very actionable requests. High-level answers below; Ben and Marissa, tagging you for precise accounting language and legal-safe phrasing.

1) Metering model: We meter on tokens produced by tokenization of the full request (input tokens + output tokens) after any automatic prefix compression. We then apply our billing quantum (25-token granularity) with a per-request minimum of 25 tokens for the hosted API. For Dedicated/Private customers we can negotiate per-call floors in the contract. Example: a huge context that compresses to 900 tokens + 400 output = 1300 total -> billed in quanta of 25 tokens (ceiling), so billed as 1325 tokens.

2) KV/prefix caching: Prefix caching reduces billable input tokens automatically if the request uses the same conversation handle and the cached KV entries are hit. For one-off long context uploads you can also upload persistent context via our context-ingest endpoint (saves as a named context id) — that will be reused without re-ingesting for subsequent calls (requires enabling context persistence on the route). I'll ask Ben to include the exact API endpoints and required headers.

3) Anchor credits: We typically apply onboarding/anchor credits as account-level credits that offset invoices until exhausted. We can structure them to apply to month 1 only, or amortize over up to 3 months depending on committed monthly spend. Marissa — what constraints do we have for multi-month credit amortization for enterprise pilots?

Quick next steps: Ben/Marissa — can you produce a 1‑pager (SOW-ready) that: (a) answers 1–3 with example calculations using their spreadsheet, (b) proposes a 3-month amortization for the onboarding credit, and (c) includes recommended hooks (context ingest flag + example curl) that Beacon can add to their integration plan.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30-min call if helpful.

— Camila Reyes

Hi all — digging into Ellie’s spreadsheet (thanks) and providing concrete math + packaging options. I attached a short table (proposed_sizing_and_credit_table.pdf) with worked examples; below are the rules we use and three product-friendly options Beacon can choose from.

Billing rules (canonical):
- Tokenization: We tokenize input + output using our standard tokenizer.
- Automatic compression: We apply prefix compression heuristics server-side before token counting; if cached fragments match, those tokens are not recounted.
- Quantum/rounding: We bill in 25-token quanta, rounding up each request's final token count to the nearest quantum.
- Per-request floor (hosted): 25 tokens. Dedicated: configurable.
- Pricing: per-token price is multiplied by the rounded billable tokens. Credits subtract at invoice level.

Three options for Beacon:
A) Default hosted terms (minimal changes) — you get account-level onboarding credit of $20k applied to invoices until used. Billing as above; no contract changes.
B) 3-month amortized anchor (recommended for pilot) — $20k credit amortized across months 1–3 as a monthly $6.67k offset; we cap amortization to up to 150% of expected monthly commit, but credits still applied as invoice offsets. This requires a short SOW clause.
C) Commit + floor (enterprise) — 6‑month guaranteed monthly commit (higher commit gets lower per-token price) + configurable per-call floor for Dedicated: e.g., 500-token floor per request for curated batch pipelines. This requires Dedicated or Private deployment and legal review.

Worked example (from their sheet):
- Example request: 900 input tokens (after compression) + 400 output = 1300 tokens -> rounded up to 1325 tokens -> billed units = 1325 / 25 = 53 quanta.
- If Beacon is on a $0.0008/per-token list price -> billed amount = 1325 * $0.0008 = $1.06 (pre-discount).

Marissa — please add compliance/legal language about whether amortized credits need to be escrowed or can be account credits, and confirm tax/invoice handling.

— Ben
Sales Operations | Redwood Inference

Thanks — summarized legal/billing-safe language below that we can paste into the SOW. I also confirmed tax treatment with finance; credits are applied net of tax where allowed and we will include line-item credit entries on each invoice while credits remain.

SOW language (draft):
"Metering and Credits: Redwood meters usage per request as the sum of input and output tokens after automatic server-side prefix compression and tokenization. Billable tokens are rounded up to the nearest 25-token quantum. For hosted customers, a minimum of 25 billable tokens per request applies. Account-level onboarding credits will be applied to invoices until exhausted. If the parties elect to amortize an onboarding credit across multiple billing periods, the credit shall be applied as an invoice-level offset in equal monthly installments, subject to a cap equal to 150% of the customer's expected monthly commit. Credits have no cash value and are non-transferable. Additional commercial commitments (e.g., Dedicated capacity or minimum monthly spend) will be documented in a separate ordering document and may alter per-token pricing and per-request floors."

Operational notes:
- For prefix caching to take effect, Beacon should use the context-ingest flow and reference the returned context_id in subsequent calls. We'll include a docs snippet.
- We cannot escrow credits in our books; credits remain an invoiced offset.

Ellie — if that language works, I can produce a one-page SOW attachment for you that Beacon legal can attach to its PO.

— Marissa
Director, Billing | Redwood Inference

Hi Ellie — looping in Customer Success for operational onboarding. Quick proposal from our side to keep rollout low-risk:

1) Pilot: 60-day pilot using hosted API with context-ingest for a select set of workflows (we'll help with the ingestion scripts).
2) Credit structure: Apply the $20k anchor as a 3-month amortized account credit (as Ben proposed) with a monthly usage cap to make overage behavior predictable.
3) Metrics: We'll track effective per-session billable tokens, cache hit rate, and tail latency for long contexts. We propose weekly syncs for the first 6 weeks.
